citation: Thomson, Iain (2001). Heidegger on Ontological Education, or: How We Become What We Are. Inquiry, 44(3), 243-268.
discipline: philosophy (Heidegger studies, philosophy of education); no empirical, affective-science, or attention-science content
thesis: Heidegger's philosophy of education is a double deconstruction: a negative moment tracing the university's contemporary crisis (instrumentalization, professionalization, vocationalization, corporatization, technologization) back to an underlying ontohistorical logic of 'enframing' (das Gestell), and a positive moment recovering, from Plato's allegory of the cave, a forgotten 'essence of paideia' -- education as the soul's transformative turning-around, not information transfer -- capable of reorienting education against this technologized drift and of re-essentializing the currently empty ideal of 'excellence' so as to reunify teaching and research and heal the university's disciplinary fragmentation.

sections.title: I. Introduction
sections.summary: Frames Heidegger's 'deconstruction' of education as inseparably negative (clearing distorting interpretations) and positive (recovering primordial experiences); previews the essay's double 'future need' (critical diagnostic perspective + positive alternative) structuring sections II-III.

sections.title: II. Heidegger's Ontohistorical Critique of the Technologization of Education (overview)
sections.summary: Argues our changing historical understanding of 'education' is grounded in the history of being (Seinsgeschichte); our own epoch, 'enframing,' reduces entities to optimizable resources, and this logic explains the university's fragmentation and instrumentalization.

sections.title: II.1 From the Essence of Truth to the History of Being
sections.summary: Explains Heidegger's technical, verbal sense of 'essence' (Wesen) against Kripke's rigid-designator conception; traces how 'the essence of truth' (aletheia) becomes 'the history of being,' a series of ontotheologically grounded historical epochs.

sections.title: II.2 The History of Being as the Ground of Education
sections.summary: Argues metaphysics determines the basic presuppositions of 'what is,' including 'education'; identifies our epoch as 'enframing' (das Gestell), grounded in a Nietzschean ontotheology of will-to-power that reduces entities to 'resources' (Bestand).

sections.title: II.3 Education as Enframing
sections.summary: Reads the 1929 Inaugural Lecture's claim that 'the rootedness of the sciences...has dried up and died' as an early diagnosis of the fragmented 'Multi-versity' (Clark Kerr); credits and then contests Bill Readings' and Timothy Clark's materialist accounts for lacking Heidegger's ontohistorical explanation and collapsing into cynicism.

sections.title: III. Heidegger's Return to Plato's Cave (overview)
sections.summary: Reconstructs 'the essence of paideia' from 'Plato's Teaching on Truth' as a four-stage pedagogy of ontological freedom, culminating in the teacher's return to the cave; develops teaching as 'letting learn.'

sections.title: III.1 Ontological Education Against Enframing
sections.summary: Genuine education 'lays hold of the soul itself' rather than filling an empty container with information; recovers the twofold sense of Bildung (forming + measure-giving pre-conception, Vor-bild) against its contrast term apaideusia.

sections.title: III.2 The Pedagogy of Ontological Freedom
sections.summary: Maps Plato's cave onto four pedagogical stages: captivity to shadows/resources; negative freedom (recognizing the fire as enframing); positive freedom/dwelling (ascent into the open); return to the cave to teach, where learning culminates in teaching.

sections.title: III.3 What Is Called Teaching?
sections.summary: Develops teaching (lehren) as fundamentally a 'letting learn' (lernen lassen), harder than mere instructing (belehren) because the teacher must be more teachable than the students; defines learning as bringing what we do into co-respondence with what addresses us as essential.

sections.title: IV. Conclusion: Envisioning a University of Teachers
sections.summary: Argues re-essentializing 'excellence' (arete) as cultivation of Dasein's world-disclosive essence could reunite teaching and research (since all positive sciences rest on unexamined ontological posits) and restore substantive shared purpose to the fragmented university community.

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: not genuinely treated; the cave's first-stage 'engrossment' in shadows superficially resembles attentional capture but is an ontological (mode-of-revealing) claim, not an attentional-cognitive one -- flagged as a false friend, not counted

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: not genuinely treated; 'dwelling' and stage-three 'positive freedom' gesture toward an absorbed comportment toward beings, but this is presented as ontological disclosedness, not flow-theoretic engagement/absorption -- no construct-level claim made

constructs.label: monotony / meaninglessness
constructs.treatment: the one construct genuinely and substantially treated: enframing's 'limitless quantification' reduces entities (including students/teachers) to optimizable 'resources' lacking intrinsic meaning, producing an 'ontological drift toward meaninglessness' increasingly obscured by information overload

constructs.label: temporality of boredom (time-drag)
constructs.treatment: not treated; Heideggerian historicity (Seinsgeschichte, ek-sistence) is discussed extensively but as historical-epochal temporality, not lived boredom-time

readings.claim: Heidegger's 'history of being' grounds our historically changing understanding of 'education,' since metaphysics supplies the basic presuppositions of 'what is' that any regional understanding (including the educational) presupposes.

Our own epoch, 'enframing,' is grounded in an 'unthought' Nietzschean ontotheology of beings as eternally recurring will-to-power; this drives the transformation of all entities, including students and teachers, into optimizable 'resources.'

Heidegger's 1929 diagnosis of hyper-specialization and lost 'rootedness' anticipates the fragmented 'Multi-versity' later diagnosed by Readings and Clark, but those later critics lack Heidegger's ontohistorical framework and slide into cynicism about the university's future.
Kripke's rigid-designator conception of essence is inapplicable to Heidegger's verbal, historical sense of Wesen ('essence' as how beings 'essence' or 'remain in play').

The recovered 'essence of paideia' -- genuine education as soul-transforming turning-around, not information transmission into an 'empty container' -- is Heidegger's positive alternative, read out of a four-stage pedagogy of ontological freedom in Plato's cave allegory.

Teaching (lehren) is 'letting learn' (lernen lassen), harder than learning because the teacher must be an exemplary, ever-more-teachable learner; 'instructing' (belehren) models education as information transfer and perpetuates enframing.

Re-essentializing 'excellence' as Aristotelian arete -- cultivating Dasein's world-disclosive essence -- could reunify teaching and research and restore substantive shared purpose to the fragmented university community.

concepts.term: deconstruction as recovery, not destruction (Destruktion vs. Zerstorung)

interlocutors.name: Plato
interlocutors.role: Republic Book VII allegory of the cave; founding pedagogical text disclosing (and, per Heidegger, ambiguating) the essence of paideia

interlocutors.name: Werner Jaeger
interlocutors.role: philological source establishing paideia as key term; flagged for uncomfortable resonance with Nazi-adjacent vitalist rhetoric in his own Paideia

interlocutors.name: Bill Readings
interlocutors.role: contested interlocutor: The University in Ruins' materialist account of Bildung's obsolescence, judged diagnostically useful but explanatorily insufficient next to Heidegger's ontohistorical account

interlocutors.name: Timothy Clark
interlocutors.role: cited alongside Readings on the 'university of excellence' as empty, self-perpetuating bureaucratic ideal

interlocutors.name: Saul Kripke
interlocutors.role: contested interlocutor: rigid-designator conception of essence, contrasted with Heidegger's verbal/historical sense of Wesen

interlocutors.name: Andrew Feenberg
interlocutors.role: contested interlocutor: 'Hegelian misinterpretation' of Heidegger's understanding of essence

interlocutors.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
interlocutors.role: ontotheological source of enframing: beings as such conceived as eternally recurring will-to-power

interlocutors.name: Jacques Derrida
interlocutors.role: 'phoenix motif' reading of Heidegger's Inaugural Lecture; restages the lecture in his own 'The Principle of Reason'

interlocutors.name: Wilhelm von Humboldt
interlocutors.role: humanist ideal linking 'objective Wissenschaft' to 'subjective Bildung'; historical unifying strategy Heidegger's re-ontologized education recombines

interlocutors.name: Clark Kerr
interlocutors.role: coined 'Multi-versity' for the internally fragmented, uni-versity-in-name-only Heidegger's 1929 diagnosis anticipates

interlocutors.name: Fichte / Schelling (German Idealists)
interlocutors.role: believed university unity would follow organically from the system of knowledge; historically superseded by Humboldt's Bildung ideal

interlocutors.name: Immanuel Kant
interlocutors.role: The Conflict of the Faculties; argued the philosophy faculty should be free and subject only to reason, background to Fichte's Berlin model

tensions.axis: deconstruction as destruction (Zerstorung) vs. deconstruction as recovery (Destruktion)
tensions.note: Thomson insists Heidegger's Destruktion of education has an inseparable positive (recovery) moment alongside its negative (clearing-away) moment, against a polemical reduction of deconstruction to mere destruction.

tensions.axis: modern/subjective Bildung (cultivation of 'subjective qualities') vs. restored measure-giving 'essence of paideia'
tensions.note: Heidegger dismisses the 19th-century misinterpretation of Bildung as deliberate cultivation of subjective qualities while insisting the word, once given back its 'original naming power,' comes closest to paideia.

tensions.axis: Readings' materialist/cynical diagnosis vs. Heidegger's ontohistorical diagnosis-with-hope
tensions.note: Readings' account of Bildung's obsolescence (an 'implacable bourgeois economic revolution') leads him to a cynicism offering only 'pragmatic' situational responses; Thomson argues Heidegger's ontohistorical account is more satisfactory and retains a positive vision.

tensions.axis: teaching (lehren, letting-learn) vs. instructing (belehren, information transfer)
tensions.note: Thomson's central pedagogical distinction: genuine teaching lets students learn to learn, rather than filling them with information as if inscribing a tabula rasa.

Two historically failed strategies for unifying the university that Heidegger's re-ontologized education recombines (shared commitment to forming excellent individuals + shared recognition of a common ontological-investigative task).
